// ledger.go
package inventory

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strings"
)

// Item is one stock line in a warehouse bin.
type Item struct {
	SKU      string   `json:"sku"`
	Name     string   `json:"name"`
	Quantity int      `json:"quantity"`
	Bins     []string `json:"bins"`
	Tags     []string `json:"tags,omitempty"`
}

// Ledger keeps stock lines keyed by SKU.
type Ledger struct {
	items map[string]*Item
}

// NewLedger returns an empty ledger ready for use.
func NewLedger() *Ledger {
	return &Ledger{items: make(map[string]*Item)}
}

// Add inserts an item or merges quantities into an existing SKU.
func (l *Ledger) Add(item Item) error {
	if strings.TrimSpace(item.SKU) == "" {
		return errors.New("sku is required")
	}
	if item.Quantity < 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("quantity for %s must not be negative: %d", item.SKU, item.Quantity)
	}
	existing, ok := l.items[item.SKU]
	if !ok {
		copied := item
		l.items[item.SKU] = &copied
		return nil
	}
	existing.Quantity += item.Quantity
	existing.Bins = mergeSorted(existing.Bins, item.Bins)
	return nil
}

// Remove reduces stock for a SKU and refuses to go below zero.
func (l *Ledger) Remove(sku string, quantity int) error {
	item, ok := l.items[sku]
	if !ok {
		return fmt.Errorf("unknown sku %q", sku)
	}
	if quantity > item.Quantity {
		return fmt.Errorf("remove %d from %s: only %d in stock", quantity, sku, item.Quantity)
	}
	item.Quantity -= quantity
	return nil
}

// Snapshot returns a copy of every item, sorted by SKU.
func (l *Ledger) Snapshot() []Item {
	skus := make([]string, 0, len(l.items))
	for sku := range l.items {
		skus = append(skus, sku)
	}
	sort.Strings(skus)
	out := make([]Item, 0, len(skus))
	for _, sku := range skus {
		out = append(out, *l.items[sku])
	}
	return out
}

// MarshalJSON writes the snapshot as a JSON array.
func (l *Ledger) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
	return json.Marshal(l.Snapshot())
}

func mergeSorted(a, b []string) []string {
	seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(a)+len(b))
	for _, v := range append(append([]string{}, a...), b...) {
		seen[v] = struct{}{}
	}
	merged := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
	for v := range seen {
		merged = append(merged, v)
	}
	sort.Strings(merged)
	return merged
}

  "reorder": {

  "items": [
    {"sku": "BLT-204", "name": "Steel bolt M8", "quantity": 480, "bins": ["A1", "A2"]},

    {"sku": "NUT-330", "name": "Lock nut M8", "quantity": 0, "bins": [], "tags": ["discontinued"]},

}
